html:
Question 1

A shipping company’s management noted that the growth of a ship’s speed is directly proportional to the difference between the ship’s maximum cruising speed and its current speed. Let V(t) be the speed of the ship, measured in kilometers per hour, and let t≥0 be the time in hours. If the maximum cruising speed of the ship is 90 km/h, which differential equation could be used to model the ship’s speed? Assume that k>0 is a constant of proportionality.

a
 dVdt=k(90−V)
b
 dVdt=−k(90+V)
c
 dVdt=kV(90−V)
d
 dVdt=−k(90−V)
e
 dVdt=kV2(90−V)
